Investigation result: this is a mise bug, not merely a missing `--no-truncate` flag.

- `MiseTable` defaults `truncate` to `false` and exposes `.truncate(true)`, but [`add_row()` always applies `row.max_height(1)`](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/9f0e/mise/src/ui/table.rs:112), causing unconditional ellipsis truncation.
- `dotfiles status` never opts into truncation ([status.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/9f0e/mise/src/cli/dotfiles/status.rs:178)).
- Only `mise ls` and `mise config ls` explicitly call `.truncate(true)`, confirming that truncation was meant to be opt-in.
- This inconsistency dates back to the table abstraction’s introduction in [PR #3561](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/3561).

The [existing discussion reply](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13106) offers valid workarounds:

```sh
MISE_TERM_WIDTH=240 mise bootstrap dotfiles status
mise bootstrap dotfiles status --json
```

But `MISE_TERM_WIDTH` only postpones truncation; it does not disable it.

Recommended resolution: fix `MiseTable` so the stored `truncate` setting actually controls the one-line row limit. Then `dotfiles status` will wrap long paths naturally, while the two commands that explicitly request truncation retain their current behavior. This deserves a central renderer regression test plus a focused dotfiles-status test. I made no changes.

[settings]

truncate = settings.truncate && !--no-truncate && !detected_agent
